items.text: REFERENCE CHANGED TO NEW YORK CITY EDUCATION
AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO NEW YORK CITY EDUCATION

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to the submission of requests
to the committee on special education for the educational services mandated by
an individualized education services program
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1325

SPONSOR: HOYLMAN-SIGAL
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law, in relation to the submission of
requests to the committee on special education for the educational
services mandated by an individualized education services program

 
PURPOSE::

To address procedural barriers that have prevented students with disa-
bilities attending nonpublic schools from accessing their entitled
educational services.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS::

Section 1 amends § 3602-c of the Education Law by adding a new subdivi-
sion 2-d, comprised of the following paragraphs:

2-d(a) provides that parents or guardians of students with disabilities
attending nonpublic schools shall have until April 1, 2025 to submit
requests for educational services for the 2024-2025 school year.

2-d(b) defines the term "procedural grounds."

2-d(c) provides that, within 14 days of the effective date of this act,
school districts shall afford parents or guardians of students whose
requests for the 2024-2025 school year were denied on procedural grounds
a reasonable opportunity to remedy their applications.

2-d(d) provides that school districts shall authorize services for the
2024-2025 school year within 14 days of receiving a procedurally suffi-
cient application.

2-d(e) provides that for students previously the subject of a due proc-
ess hearing regarding service rates under § 4404 of the Education Law,
school districts shall authorize the hourly rate established in that
determination without requiring new proceedings.

2-d(f) empowers parents or guardians who obtained equivalent services
due to procedural denials during the 2023-2024 or 2024-2025 school years
to seek reimbursement for costs incurred.

2-d(g) empowers parents or guardians to seek compensatory services for
students denied services on procedural grounds during the 2023-2024 or
2024-2025 school years.

2-d(h) prohibits conditioning special educational services mandated
under § 3602 of the Education Law on the waiver of procedural safe-
guards.

2-d(i) sets forth that school districts shall notify all parents or
guardians of nonpublic school students with disabilities of the
provisions of this act within 14 days of its effective date.

Section 2 sets forth the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION::
Students with disabilities attending nonpublic schools in New York are
entitled to equitable access to educational services under the state's
Education Law § 3602-c. However, for the 20242025 school year, school
districts adopted strict enforcement policies that created unprecedented
barriers for families to obtain services. These policies were ostensibly
intended to reduce administrative burdens, but were implemented without
adequate notice or support for families.  As a result, thousands of
eligible students were denied critical educational services due to minor
and uncommunicated technical deficiencies. These measures forced fami-
lies to shoulder the burdens of an inefficient system, with the conse-
quences falling hardest on vulnerable children whose education was
unjustly denied. When services are delayed or denied, students lose
critical support necessary for their academic success and development.
Families often also bear a significant financial burden, paying out-of-
pocket for services that are typically publicly funded.

This bill would provide a temporary, targeted solution for students
impacted in the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 school years. Specifically, it
would extend the deadline for families to request services for the
2024-2025 school year to April 1, 2025, affording them time to address
procedural errors. School districts would be required to notify families
of deficiencies in their applications, provide clear instructions for
corrections, and allow resubmissions. Services would be authorized with-
in 14 days of receiving a complete application. To reduce administrative
burdens, districts would honor rates established in prior due process
hearings without requiring new proceedings. Families who incurred costs
for equivalent services during the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 school years
would be empowered to seek reimbursement, and students denied services
would be empowered to seek compensatory education to address the harm
caused. This bill would also ensure that families retain their legal
protections by prohibiting districts from conditioning services on the
waiver of due process rights.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY::

None.   
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE::

This act shall take effect immediately.

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1325B

SPONSOR: HOYLMAN-SIGAL
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law, in relation to the submission of
requests to the committee on special education for the educational
services mandated by an individualized education services program

 
PURPOSE:

To address procedural barriers that have prevented students with disa-
bilities attending nonpublic schools from accessing their entitled
educational services.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends § 3602-c of the Education Law by adding new subdivision
2-d and 2-e, comprised of the following paragraphs:

2-d(a) requires annual notice from school districts about special educa-
tion service application processes and deadlines.

2-d(b) provides that, if school district notice is delayed, parents
shall have at least 28 days from receipt of proper notice to submit
requests for special education services.

2-d(c) prohibits conditioning special educational services mandated
under § 3602 of the Education Law on the waiver of procedural safe-
guards.

2-e(a) establishes that provisions of this subdivision apply exclusively
to the city school district of New York City for the 2024-2025 school
year.

2-e(b) defines the term "procedural grounds."

2-e(c) requires school districts to notify parents of nonpublic school
students with disabilities of the process to request services and
provide them an opportunity to submit or correct applications previously
denied.

2-e(d) empowers parents or guardians to seek compensatory services for
students denied services on procedural grounds.

2-e(e) sets forth that school districts shall incorporate compensatory
services into the student's individualized education service program.

Section 2 sets forth the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Students with disabilities attending nonpublic schools in New York are
entitled to equitable access to educational services under the state's
Education Law § 3602-c. However, for the 20242025 school year, school
districts adopted strict enforcement policies that created unprecedented
barriers for families to obtain services. These policies were ostensibly
intended to reduce administrative burdens, but were implemented without
adequate notice or support for families.  As a result, thousands of
eligible students were denied critical educational services due to minor
and uncommunicated technical deficiencies. These measures forced fami-
lies to shoulder the burdens of an inefficient system, with the conse-
quences falling hardest on vulnerable children whose education was
unjustly denied. When services are delayed or denied, students lose
critical support necessary for their academic success and development.

This bill addresses these challenges through permanent statewide meas-
ures and temporary provisions for New York City. It creates a statewide
requirement for clear, timely, and annual notice to parents regarding
the application process for special education services, along with
provisions to extend application deadlines if districts fail to provide
timely notice. It explicitly prohibits school districts from condition-
ing the provision of services on a waiver of procedural safeguards. For
the 2024-2025 school year in New York City, the bill additionally
requires districts to notify families who missed the opportunity to
apply for or correct their service applications due to procedural
issues, and allows parents whose children were denied mandated services
on procedural grounds to seek compensatory education to remedy lost
educational opportunities.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

None.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

C.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1325C

SPONSOR: HOYLMAN-SIGAL
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law, in relation to the submission of
requests to the committee on special education for the educational
services mandated by an individualized education services program

 
PURPOSE:

To address procedural barriers that have prevented students with disa-
bilities attending nonpublic schools from accessing their entitled
educational services.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends § 3602-c of the Education Law by adding new subdivi-
sions 2-d and 2-e, comprised of the following paragraphs:

2-d requires annual notice from school districts about special education
service application processes and deadlines.

2-e(a) establishes that provisions of this subdivision apply exclusively
to the city school district of New York City for the 2024-25 school
year.

2-e(b) allows parents whose children received some or none of the recom-
mended services on their Individualized Education Service Program (IESP)
for the 2024-25 school year, because a June 1 request was not filed, to
request an expedited annual review, which the committee must conduct
within 60 calendar days. At that review, parents may submit evidence of
impacted educational progress; the committee must consider the impact of
the missed services and incorporate any impact into a new IESP.

Section 2 sets forth the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Students with disabilities attending nonpublic schools in New York are
entitled to equitable access to educational services under the state's
Education Law § 3602-c. However, for the 202425 school year, school
districts adopted strict enforcement policies that created unprecedented
barriers for families to obtain services. These policies were ostensibly
intended to reduce administrative burdens, but were implemented without
adequate notice or support for families.  As a result, thousands of
eligible students were denied critical educational services. These meas-
ures forced families to shoulder the burdens of an inefficient system,
with the consequences falling hardest on vulnerable children whose
education was unjustly denied.  When services are delayed or denied,
students lose critical support necessary for their academic success and
development.

This bill addresses these challenges through permanent statewide meas-
ures and temporary provisions for New York City. It creates a statewide
requirement for clear, timely, and annual notice to parents regarding
the application process for special education services. For the 202425
school year in New York City, it further allows parents of students who
did not receive some or all of the services in their IESP to seek an
expedited annual review for the 2025-26 school year, at which they may
present evidence of the student's impacted educational progress to be
considered in the student's new IESP.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

None.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Requires the school district of location shall annually provide written notice to all parents or persons in parental relation to students with disabilities attending nonpublic schools within their district regarding the process for requesting special education services; relates to the denial of services in a city having a population of one million or more for the 2024--2025 school year.
